subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Calibration and Confidence
description: A quick win: understand Calibration and Confidence.

hook.text: Doctors told patients surgery had a 90% success rate. Actual success was 50%. Their confidence outran reality.

buildup.text: Calibration means your confidence matches your accuracy. Say 80% sure and be right 80% of the time.

discovery.text: Most people are overconfident. They say 90% sure but are right only 70% of the time. The gap is measurable.

twist.text: Weather forecasters are well-calibrated because they get daily feedback. Most professionals never do.

climax.text: Track your confident predictions. After fifty, check the hit rate. Reality is the only calibration tool.

punchline.text: Confidence without calibration is just guessing loudly.

quiz.question: Why are weather forecasters well-calibrated?
options: They receive fast, daily feedback on predictions
They are naturally less biased than others

details.summary: Poor calibration means your confidence levels do not match your accuracy. Well-calibrated people are right 80 percent of the time when they say they are 80 percent confident. Most people are overconfident, being right far less often than their confidence suggests.
details.whyItMatters: Miscalibrated confidence leads to insufficient contingency planning, inadequate risk margins, and unpleasant surprises. Leaders who think they are 95 percent certain when they should be 60 percent certain make recklessly aggressive decisions.
takeaways: Most people are systematically overconfident in their judgments
Overconfidence narrower confidence intervals that miss the true answer
Calibration can be improved with practice and feedback on past predictions

faq.question: How do you test your own calibration?
faq.answer: Make predictions with explicit confidence levels and track your accuracy. If you say you are 90 percent confident and you are right only 60 percent of the time, you are poorly calibrated. Most people discover significant overconfidence through this exercise.

faq.question: Can calibration be improved?
faq.answer: Yes. Weather forecasters and professional predictors show excellent calibration because they receive frequent, clear feedback. Regular prediction tracking with honest comparison to outcomes gradually improves calibration for anyone willing to practice.
